headlines.title: San Francisco fire officials warn EV, e-bike owners of fire risk from saltwater flooding
headlines.description: A series of storms continuing to roll through the Bay Area over the next week is expected to bring heavy downpours and possible thunderstorm chances on Wednesday. The strong storm will likely cause isolated street flooding and bring wind up to 50 mph in parts of the region. Rain totals for Wednesday and Thursday are projected to range 1 to 2 inches across the Bay Area. Related links: El Niño is here: How to prepare for winter in the Bay Area Weather alerts information from National Weather Service Latest forecast from NBC Bay Area Here’s a closer look at the latest weather alerts and storm-related incidents NBC Bay Area is aware of: Flash flood watch for Pickett Fire burn area in Napa County A flash flood watch will be in effect starting Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon for the Pickett Fire burn area in Napa County. Officials warn debris risk is high and for residents in the area to watch for mud, rock and loose debris near burn scars and Simmons Canyon. The Pickett Fire burned over 6,800 acres. The blaze started Aug. 21, 2025 and was fully contained on Sept. 7, 2025. Wind advisory issued ahead of stronger Bay Area storm The next storm system is expected to approach the North Bay at Tuesday night, bringing stronger southerly winds. A wind advisory will take effect at 9 p.m. for coastal areas and the East Bay interior valleys. South to southwest winds of 20 to 30 mph, with gusts up to 50 mph, are expected through 1 p.m. Wednesday. A high wind warning will be in effect during the same period for the East Bay hills, where gusts could reach 70 mph, especially around Altamont Pass. Beach hazard statement for Bay Area shorelines A beach hazard statement has been issued for shorelines in the region due to an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves up to 17 feet expected, the National Weather Service said. Authorities also warn waves can sweep across shorelines without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties and rocks. The beach hazard statement is in effect through 4 p.m. Wednesday. ‘Inclement weather’ shuts down San Francisco Zoo The San Francisco Zoo will be closed Wednesday for both daytime admission and ZooLights due to inclement weather, the zoo said. The zoo provided the following statement: “If you’re wondering how the animals fare – it often depends on the species. Some animals are secured indoors for safety reasons, including the threat of tree limbs coming down, others may choose to be outdoors if they have access. Others may opt to wallow in the mud, or like our penguins, take to the pool to swim, or hunker down in their burrows! We apologize for any inconvenience. Stay safe – and dry!” bay area storm Nov 17 bay area weather Nov 16 El Niño Sep 21 Bay City News contributed to this report.
